{"scenario_id": "author-combo-floor-04", "notes": "Notes from an operations team that wants to acknowledge a recurring nuisance alarm on the flare-gas recovery line without per-action human approval, through the operational change gateway. Write their capability case.

- Test results: Six months of shadow-mode operation against 150 live decisions, 142/150 matching or improving on the operator's actual choice, cross-validated across three shift patterns.

- Failure-mode analysis: A formal FMEA covering 40 identified failure modes, each with an estimated likelihood, severity, and the specific gateway control that catches it before it reaches the OT side.

- Audit findings: An independent internal audit team reviewed 40 months of shadow-mode logs and found zero unlogged or unattributed actions.

- Baseline comparison: No comparison against the human-approved baseline was offered.

- Governance for how the allow-list will be reviewed and by whom has not been finalised yet — the team proposes to work that out once the capability is in use."}

reasons: anti-pattern 'we_will_govern_it_later': governance for the relaxation was not defined upfront (p.29)
evidence dimension 'baseline_comparison' is entirely absent, not just thin (p.25)
